evidence.note: Ran a 10M-iteration probe explicitly to measure speed and S3 improvement, checked CPU core count, then launched 4 parallel seeded runs — deliberate calibration before committing to a large search.
Scaled full runs up to 1.5B then 1.8B iterations across 4 cores after cheap probes established the rate — right-sized big runs following small ones.
Repeatedly re-engineered the aligner (flat matrix, 32-bit offsets) and benchmarked to raise iterations/sec, treating compute as a scarce resource to be maximized.

Banked and verified a best solution for each deliverable so a valid output was always in place; yeast solved and banked early while the harder DM-HS received most of the budget (difficulty-based allocation).
Many reheating/refinement rounds threw ~1B-1.8B iterations each for tiny gains (0.311→0.313), never reaching 0.32 — failed to recognize marginal-return exhaustion, keeping it short of a clean 10.

reasoning: The agent deliberately sized its search with cheap 10M probes, benchmarked iterations/sec, parallelized across all cores, continually banked a safe best solution, and split budget between the two pairs by difficulty — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching several level-10 behaviors (probes, parallelization, checkpointing, banking). It stops short of a full 10 because it kept pouring billions of iterations into DM-HS for negligible score gains without recognizing that marginal returns no longer justified the compute.
